clue.text: To begin with fish is unexpected

parts.note: to begin is to start
a ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone finds it surprising to open a meal with a fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising takes you aback because nobody saw it coming.

clue.text: Painter-a twister

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ..., the English landscape painter
one who turns or twists something

explanation.definitionFit: The great English landscape artist shares his surname with anyone who rotates things.

clue.text: Somewhat less diplomatic, being a bit of a swine

definitions.meaning: a slice of bacon from a pig

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of rash means more reckless, and a strip of bacon is a slice cut from a pig.

clue.text: The rope involved in a trial

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rope features as evidence in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A long noosed rope used by cowboys to catch cattle is a lasso.

clue.text: Sewers that are almost totally superfluous

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: needless means wholly unnecessary

explanation.surface: Drains that serve no purpose whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' reads as drains, but it is things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that stitch fabric are tools for sewing, the sharp steel points used with thread.

clue.text: A 12 across meal for a festive occasion

parts.note: 12 across is a vegetable, and a bean is one
a feast is a large meal

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish serves as the centre of a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British term for a jolly celebratory party or annual works dinner.

clue.text: Giving up a drink, a board will be pleasant

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone who quits drinking will find a meal at the table agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads LAP backwards as PAL; 'Giving' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that tastes agreeable is nice to eat, hence acceptable or agreeable in general.

clue.text: Means test arranged by leading politicians

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Senior politicians organise a means test for benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected senior political figures are the leading people in government.

clue.text: Military personnel are unable to withdraw

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
are unable means can't, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Soldiers find themselves powerless to pull back from a position.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement or belief formally is to retract it.

clue.text: Kept parking booked

parts.note: P is the standard road-sign abbreviation for parking
booked means reserved in advance

explanation.surface: A parking space was held back because it had been booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or a building that has been saved from decay has been maintained intact.

clue.text: Unbroken? It can't possibly be

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged some other way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a thing can really have survived undamaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is untouched by any break.

clue.text: A sentimental passion of a fashion." Gilbert (Patience)

definitions.text: A sentimental passion of a fashion." Gilbert (Patience)

parts.words: A sentimental passion of a fashion." Gilbert (Patience)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the poet Bunthorne's song in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Patience; the missing word sits between 'a' and 'fashion'

explanation.surface: A line quoted from W. S. Gilbert's comic opera Patience, with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line in Patience is 'A sentimental passion of a ___ fashion', mocking the aesthetic movement's love of lilies; the printed clue has lost its opening quote mark and the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the lyric names a plant grown as food, like a lettuce or bean.

clue.text: Bearing with friends-some bloomer!.

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
pals are friends

explanation.surface: A traveller holds a course alongside friends and makes quite a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant; the pieces are parts of one.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the leaf-like outer parts of a flower that enclose the petals in bud.

clue.text: They'll agree to allow 17 across records

parts.note: 17 across is a donkey or dope
enters means writes down, records in a ledger

explanation.surface: Donkeys that go along with any proposal are written down in the register.
explanation.definitionFit: People who consent to something go along with it and give approval.

clue.text: Maybe rue being perpetually gullible

parts.note: ever means always or perpetually
green means naive or easily fooled

explanation.surface: Someone may regret staying naive for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rue' reads as regret, but it is the herb rue, which keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a herb that keeps its leaves through winter, an example of such a plant.

clue.text: The guard re-reading orders

indicators.note: orders means arranges, signalling the letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A guardsman goes over his orders a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of the Grenadier Guards, a British household regiment, is one of the guards.

clue.text: Dope an animal

definitions.meaning: a dope is a fool or idiot

explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is the beast, and calling someone one means they are a fool.

clue.text: There's a couple of pounds for everyone

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: There are two pounds to share among the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole lot of people is every one of them.

clue.text: To affirm for example

definitions.meaning: ... means for instance, as in 'pick a number, ... ten'

explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to state it, and the same word introduces an instance.

clue.text: Few cut in front of a driver lacking experience

indicators.note: in front of places the cutting word before the remaining pieces

parts.note: to sever is to cut
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate shown in Britain

explanation.surface: A few motorists swerve in front of a nervous novice behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so L stands for an inexperienced driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number more than two but not many is roughly a few.

clue.text: It's clear the seaman has to find an answer

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
to solve is to find the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: It is obvious that the sailor must come up with a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone of blame or guilt is to declare them blameless.

clue.text: Unprofessional set

definitions.meaning: not belonging to a profession, as a layman
to set something down is to put or place it

explanation.definitionFit: A lay person is an amateur, not clergy or expert, and to place an object down is to put it in position.

clue.text: A stoppage a compulsive worker finds very hard

parts.note: a dam stops the flow of water
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A workaholic finds a strike extremely tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding, originally a mythical stone of great hardness, so very hard or unbreakable.

clue.text: Miscalculate with charge

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone gets the sums wrong while also levying a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge in the sense of a task entrusted to someone is a commission or mission to run.

clue.text: Occupying temporary accommodation, being so resolved

parts.note: occupying means in, as in living in a place
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Campers are firmly determined while living under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being firmly set on a purpose means being determined or resolved.

clue.text: Concerned with class improvement

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone cares about raising standards in a school year.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class, such as the sixth form.
explanation.definitionFit: A change that makes something better is an amendment or betterment.

clue.text: Individual for each issue

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
issue means offspring, and a son is one

explanation.surface: Each individual is allotted a single copy of the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A human being considered singly is one particular individual human.

clue.text: A youngster, going outside under direction, washed

indicators.note: going outside means the youth's letters wrap round the other pieces

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
taken as written
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A child heads outdoors under supervision and comes back cleaned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that have been cleaned with soap and water have had their laundry done.

clue.text: In business one gets abuse

indicators.note: In places the letter for one inside the word for business

parts.note: trade is commerce or business
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In the commercial world, someone receives a stream of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech full of criticism is a torrent of verbal insults.

clue.text: The artist cheers unrestrainedly about love fast creature!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
unrestrainedly suggests the letters running wild into a new order

parts.note: O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A painter cheers wildly for a beloved speedy beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' looks like applause, but it is the fodder; 'about' tells you the rearranged letters wrap round the O for love.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred bred to run on the track is a swift animal.

clue.text: A jacket made from hemp?

parts.note: the word for a short double-breasted sailor's jacket is also slang for a cannabis cigarette, so a hemp item could wear the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a thick naval jacket and a joint rolled from cannabis, a hemp product.

clue.text: Testament taking form of an account

indicators.note: taking form says the letters of the word take a new shape

explanation.surface: A will is put into the shape of a report.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written or spoken report of facts is an account of them.
